name: Pantoprazole
summary: The PPI most often reached for in polypharmacy and inpatient settings because of its comparatively clean interaction profile.
good: Patients on interacting drugs (clopidogrel, warfarin, HIV antivirals), ICU/inpatient acid suppression, stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
bad: No strong reason to avoid it; occasionally less familiar to patients than omeprazole/esomeprazole for OTC use.
clinicalPearls: This is the PPI to reach for first whenever the question is "will this interact with the rest of the regimen?"
mechanism: Irreversible H⁺/K⁺-ATPase inhibition, same as other PPIs.
pharmacodynamics: Comparable to omeprazole; slightly lower affinity for off-target CYP enzymes translates to fewer interaction concerns rather than a potency difference.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Standard PPI onset — days to full effect with regular dosing.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: CYP2C19 and CYP3A4, but with lower relative affinity, so it is less likely to meaningfully inhibit the metabolism of co-administered drugs.

indications: GERD, erosive esophagitis, H. pylori regimens, and the dominant IV PPI for acute upper GI bleeding.
interactionNotes: Fewest clinically significant CYP-mediated interactions among the PPIs — a major reason it is favored in patients on clopidogrel, warfarin, or complex regimens.
